name: Quarter-ton truck (jeep)
about: Made by tools/battle-models (car). Metres; x forward, y right, z up. A battle model: `part` says which part each point belongs to; `parts` are the parts (parent, pivot, axis of turning, way of sliding); `sockets` are named places for flash, smoke, fire and wake; `clips` move the parts. Turns: +t degrees about an axis carries p to p cos t + (axis x p) sin t + axis (axis . p)(1 - cos t), about the part's pivot. Paints: 0 upper, 1 upper2, 2 shade, 3 track, 4 rubber, 5 steel, 6 bright, 7 wood, 8 canvas, 9 glass, 10 black, 11 rust, 12 lamp, 13 white, 14 red, 15 yellow, 16 blue, 17 leather, 18 torn, 19 rope, 20 cloth, 21 skin, 22 brass `mid`: the middle mesh, for about 40 to 140 m (~15,000 triangles): the near mesh thinned, small pieces gone, the far mesh's track band in place of the links, alike parts (road wheels) carrying the same mesh; its `part` numbers count the parts without the track links, as `far`'s do.

parts.name: vehicle
parts.note: on the ground under her middle; the game moves and turns this

parts.name: hull
parts.note: rocks on her springs: + nose up (clips also roll and bob her)

parts.name: steer_l
parts.note: a front wheel on its kingpin: + steers to the right

parts.name: steer_r
parts.note: a front wheel on its kingpin: + steers to the right

parts.name: screen
parts.note: the windscreen on its hinges at the cowl: built folded flat forward on the bonnet; + raises it (92 stands it up, leaning back a little)

parts.name: mg_mount
parts.note: the machine gun on its post: + swings it to the right; the game aims it while a man has hold of it

parts.name: mg_cradle
parts.note: the gun tips on its trunnions: + muzzle up

sockets.name: hook
sockets.note: the pintle: a 37 mm gun's or a trailer's eye goes on it

sockets.name: grip.gunner.l
sockets.note: the gunner's left hand on the gun

sockets.name: grip.gunner.r
sockets.note: the gunner's right hand on the gun

sockets.name: driver
sockets.note: the driver, seated: the top of his seat, 0.32 over the floor his boots are on (the footwell runs on to the firewall 0.77 ahead); his hands on grip.driver.l and grip.driver.r

sockets.name: grip.driver.l
sockets.note: the driver's left hand on the wheel's rim

sockets.name: grip.driver.r
sockets.note: the driver's right hand on the wheel's rim

sockets.name: rider.1
sockets.note: the man beside the driver, seated (the top of his seat, as the driver's; his hands free)

sockets.name: rider.2
sockets.note: a man on the seat behind, seated facing ahead: the top of his seat, 0.38 over the floor

sockets.name: rider.3
sockets.note: a man on the seat behind, seated facing ahead

sockets.name: gunner
sockets.note: the gunner's feet, on the floor behind the front seats (in place of rider.2 and rider.3): he stands, his hands on grip.gunner.l and grip.gunner.r about 0.9 up, and turns his body with the gun

sockets.name: engine
sockets.note: the bonnet: smoke and the first fire

start.about: the engine is started: she shudders, a puff from the exhaust

drive.about: under way: the body's own motion on its springs (the game rolls and steers the wheels, runs the tracks and moves her)

move_off.about: she moves off: the nose lifts as she takes up the drive, and settles

stop.about: she brakes: start it as the brakes go on. The nose dips and stays down while she slows; she is at rest `rest` seconds in (play it faster or slower to fit), and the nose comes back up, a little over, and settles

knocked_out.about: knocked out: struck at 0.0, she sinks on a burst tyre, smoke, then fire at the engine; holds its last pose (follow with `burn`)

burn.about: burning: fire at the engine and in the body, black smoke (loop after knocked_out)

mg_burst.about: a burst from her machine gun: ten rounds

steer.what: the game steers the front wheels inside their lock: + to the right

mg.what: aimed by the game inside the two parts' limits while a man has hold of it (his hands on grip.gunner.l and grip.gunner.r): mg_mount + to the right, mg_cradle + muzzle up; with the file's `mg` swap off she has no gun: never aim it or play mg_burst. The post stands between the front seats: with the screen folded the gun fires over the bonnet; the gunner stands behind it, facing the way the gun points.

swaps.how: mg: off scales the parts of the gun to nothing (a part scaled to nothing is not drawn), and the two men behind sit on their seat.

on.what: the .30 Browning on its post (scouts, the reconnaissance troops, and many more)

off.what: no gun: a staff or liaison car

dust_is: road dirt: `dust` (0 to 100 a point) is how far the point's finished paint has gone to `dust_colour`; thick low on her, thin by her shoulders, on her tracks too. (`wear` is still paint chipped to the metal, as it was.) A mark's own `dust` dulls it the same way: paint the mark, then take it that far to `dust_colour`. Work it out on the coat she wears (after a paint swap; a swap's choice may name its own dust_colour and haze_colour), from these numbers: the .glb's COLOR_0 is the same thing worked out for the coat she was built in. A game on other ground may use that ground's own colour. Lay no other dust, sun fade or camouflage of the game's own over a file that has `dust`. `haze` (0 to 100, where the mesh has it) is the thin pale dust lying on what looks up: after `dust`, take the point that far to `haze_colour`.

dust_by_ground.how: dust_by_ground: the dirt of each ground (field, desert, italy, steppe, winter, tropic), worked out for her build coat: on a field of that ground take `dust` toward its dust_colour and `haze` toward its haze_colour in place of the file's own. A paint swap's choice that names its own dust_colour and haze_colour (her desert coat) is already worked out for its ground.

shade_is: `shade` (0 to 1 a point, where the mesh has it, as the soldiers' files have it) is how open the point is to the sky: multiply the point's finished colour by it. The shadow in her creases, which the battle's light does not cast.

running.how: turn each wheel by (distance run on its side) / radius, in radians; play tracks.left and tracks.right at (speed of that side) / stride * long

units: scouts, staffs and messengers (United States; Britain and the Commonwealth from 1942 and the Free French, in their own paint; the Soviet Union and China were lent her too); the jeep with the .30 on its post rides ahead of the American armor
